what_changed:
Replace v1 PyTorch glue chain (~10 ops: cumsum+cat, broadcast sub/exp/where,
permute/contiguous x3, bmm x2, fp32 mul, bf16 cast) with ONE Triton megakernel
parallelised over (B*K, head). Each program:

  1. tl.dot(C_g, B_g^T, out_dtype=fp32) -> G_g : 128x128 fp32 in regs

     loaded from a single host-side torch.cumsum (cheap, <= 256 KB).
  3. M = (G * L).bf16
  4. tl.dot(M, X_h, out_dtype=fp32).bf16 -> Y_h : 128x128 bf16
  5. Store Y_diag in canonical [B, K, 128, 32, 128] layout.

Eliminates 64 MiB fp32 M and 32 MiB bf16 M global tensors entirely; only X is
read per-head, B/C/prefixA per-group/head once. Grid up to 2048 blocks for full
B200 SM coverage.

+# V1: Algorithmic refactor of v0 baseline.
+#
+# v0 (= verbatim SOL reference) computes G and Y_diag with element-wise broadcasts that
+# materialize six-dimensional tensors of shape [B, K, 128, 128, 32, 128] (≈ 64 MiB F32
+# per (B·K) chunk), reducing them by `(a*b).sum(-1)` — never reaching tensor cores
+# (NCU: tensor-core util 0%, SM throughput 0.7% on the small kernels).
+#
+# This kernel exposes the op's two batched-GEMM cores directly:
+#   G_g = C_g · B_gᵀ   (per (B·K·group),  bf16 inputs, 128×128 × K=128)
+#   Y_h = M_h · X_h    (per (B·K·head),   bf16,         128×128 × K=128)
+# Three algebraic identities replace flat elementwise work:
+#   * The reference's `expand → tril → cumsum → masked_fill → exp` chain on
+#     `[B,H,K,128,128]` is exactly the closed-form decay
+#         L[i,j] = exp(prefixA[i+1] − prefixA[j+1]) · 𝟙(i ≥ j),
+#     where prefixA is the exclusive prefix-sum of A_cumsum (verified locally).
+#   * B, C are group-broadcast (8 groups → 32 heads), so the G GEMM is computed only
+#     once per group and broadcast 4× lazily — no `repeat_interleave` of the 128×128
+#     inputs.
+#   * G and Y are reduced over a 128-element K-dim ⇒ obvious bf16 tensor-core GEMMs.
+# bf16 contractions; SOL tolerance is `rtol=5e-2, atol=1e-5`, comfortable for bf16
+# K=128 GEMMs on B200 tensor cores.
